flags.name: Flag 1 - CF Bot Management
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, select the one-flare.com domain, navigate to Security Rules, and open the Mitigate definite bot traffic rule. Cloudflare allows users to customize their security rules. For this specific rule, what is the response code sent after blocking? The flag is the response code

hints.description: Custom block responses let you choose the status code.
It is the standard 'you are not allowed' code.
The flag is <s1-answer>403</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 2 - CF Security Insight
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, select the soledrop.co domain, open the Security dropdown and choose Security Rules, then click the Traffic Sequence button in the top right, next to Documentation. Traffic Sequence shows the simplified journey of a request as it proxies through a Cloudflare configuration. Looking at the flow, what feature is used right before a request reaches the origin server? The flag is the name of the box preceding Origin server

hints.description: The description of the rule is: to help distribute traffic between origins
The flag is <s1-answer>Load balancing</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 3 - Security Insight
flags.description: While still in the Traffic Sequence window, click on Workers, select the shop-soledrop-worker from any row, choose Metrics from the nav bar at the top, and set the event window to the last 30 days. Review the Request Distribution map. Cloudflare Workers is a serverless platform for building, deploying, and scaling apps across Cloudflare's global network without needing complex configuration. The shop.soledrop.co site from before was deployed using a custom worker. Under Request Distribution we can see the locations where a Worker ran to handle an incoming request. Find the city where this worker was deployed the most. The flag is the name of the city.

hints.description: The <s1-label>Request Distribution</s1-label> section will have an interactable globe with pins in the locations. The flag will be the top city in the list to the right of the globe.
The flag is <s1-answer>Denver</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 4 - CF HA Equivalent
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, navigate to Build from the left-hand menu, select AI from the dropdown, and open Workers AI. In the model catalog, filter for Automatic Speech Recognition. Like standard Cloudflare Workers, Workers AI allow users to deploy LLMs and AI agents across Cloudflare's global network. From the model catalog, what is the name of the model that can perform Automatic Speech Recognition? The flag is the name of the model

hints.description: There are 6 models listed on the page. The flag is the name of either of the models associated with <s1-value>Automatic Speech Recognition</s1-value>.
The flag will begin with <s1-value>assemblyai/</s1-value>...
The flag is <s1-answer>assemblyai/universal-3-pro</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 5 - AI Prompt Injection
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Alerts, filter for AI Prompt Injection, and open any matching alert to read the full name of the detection rule that raised it. Open an AI Prompt Injection alert. The detection rule's name calls out the exact API route it watches. What is that route? The flag is the API route.

hints.description: The rule name ends with the route, after the words <s1-value>SoleDrop Concierge</s1-value>.
It is a versioned API path ending in the word chat.
The flag is <s1-answer>/api/v1/chat</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 6 - Attempt
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Alerts, open an AI Prompt Injection alert, and read the Purple AI overview panel. A single source sending many chat POSTs in a short window is characteristic of what? The flag is the name of the attempt.

hints.description: It is automated trial-and-error against the prompt.
The word rhymes with 'buzzing'.
The flag is <s1-answer>Injection fuzzing</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 7 - Enrichment
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Hyperautomation, open the See WAF Rule workflow, and add the Cloudflare action named Get zero trust user failed logins. Read its default URL before filling in any values. What is the LAST path segment of that default URL? The flag is the segment.

hints.description: The URL is a template with unfilled placeholders like <s1-value>account_id</s1-value>.
It is the very end of the path, after the user id — two words joined by an underscore.
The flag is <s1-answer>failed_logins</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 8 - Default URL
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Copy the default URL from the previous question, paste it into a browser address bar exactly as-is with the placeholders still in it, and press enter.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Paste that default URL into a browser — what is the error message in the JSON body?
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="Could not ...">The flag is the error message.</s1-flag>
flags.plainAnswer: Could not route to /client/v4/accounts/account_id/access/users/user_id/failed_logins, perhaps your object identifier is invalid?

hints.description: Cloudflare's API rejects the unfilled placeholders as invalid object identifiers.
The message begins with <s1-value>Could not route to ...</s1-value> and ends by questioning your object identifier.
The flag is <s1-answer>Could not route to /client/v4/accounts/account_id/access/users/user_id/failed_logins, perhaps your object identifier is invalid?</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 9 - Failed Login Attempt
flags.description:
<s1-nav>In that same <s1-label>Hyperautomation</s1-label> action, fill in the <s1-value>account ID</s1-value> and <s1-value>user ID</s1-value> your facilitator reads out, click <s1-label>Test Action</s1-label>, and read the response.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Test the given <s1-label>Workflow</s1-label> and see the correct response when the account and user information has been input.

Which JSON key holds the time of the failed login?
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="timestamp">The flag is the JSON key.</s1-flag>

hints.description: The response is a list of failed-login records; look at the fields on one record.
It is one word, and it is not <s1-value>timestamp</s1-value>.
The flag is <s1-answer>datetime</s1-answer>.
